From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller's Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every liability and completion-protection point. Several of the departures compound one another. The general data-room disclosure, the blanket buyer-knowledge bar and the "all Claims" limitation and non-reliance language together would hollow out the warranties and could reach fraud. We should not accept any of the Seller's framing that these terms are "FINAL", "agreed at principal level" or "market standard". We should send a full mark-up at our starting positions.

---

## 1. Threshold point: the Seller's framing is not authority

- **"Settled at principal level… FINAL… not intended to be re-opened."** This is a counterparty assertion. Under playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3, it has no weight unless confirmed through our own authority process. We have no record that Amelia Frost agreed to any of these positions.
- **"Market standard" (10–20% caps, ~1% baskets, 12–18 months, buyer-knowledge bars).** This is advocacy, not fact. It does not move our positions.
- **The 20% / AUD 4.8m cap matches our fallback number.** That does not clear it. The fallback requires prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft, and none has been given.
- **Staleness.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026, which is about six weeks ago. Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006 and Sandbar all need refreshed facts. We should separate verified updates from Seller assertions.

**Action:** Confirm internally with Amelia Frost whether any principal-level discussion took place. Until then, treat every position as open.

---

## 2. Liability regime

| Issue | Seller position | Playbook | Push back |
|---|---|---|---|
| **General cap (cl 12.1)** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m; 20% fallback only with Amelia Frost's written authority (none) | Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not signal the fallback. |
| **De minimis (cl 12.2)** | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. Five times our position. Many genuine claims would fall out entirely. |
| **Basket (cl 12.2)** | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, first dollar once exceeded | Reject on both level and structure. An excess-only basket permanently writes off the first AUD 250k of loss. |
| **General claims period** | 18 months | 24 months; 18 months needs Amelia Frost's approval (none) | Counter at 24 months. |
| **"Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"** | Catch-all | No hidden general-regime override; categories kept separate | **Strike.** This drafting would quietly pull Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, covenants and payment obligations into the general caps and time limits. It is the most dangerous single sentence in the package. |

**Fundamental / Title warranties.** The Seller proposes the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity". **Reject.** Title and capacity are the core of what we are buying. They need a separate regime:
- a cap of 100% of price;
- a claims period of at least six years;
- carve-outs from the general basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.

**Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature".** As drafted, this would extend caps, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct. Our playbook treats the fraud carve-out as **non-waivable**: no one on our side can concede it. We need an express carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable. Specific indemnities, covenants and payment obligations also need to be expressly carved out of the general limitations.

**Tax / IP.** The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime". They are not settled. Our position is that they remain **open** as separate categories. We should not accept their absorption into the general regime. Equally, we should not assume any unlimited liability outcome in our favour.

---

## 3. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

**General disclosure (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2).** The Seller discloses:
- the entire data room as at 22 September (DD-002 to DD-012);
- the Accounts and statutory registers;
- all publicly searchable records.

**Reject.** This deems everything in the data room disclosed against every warranty. That would include the Bluefen consent gap, the unrepaid Riverlark facility, the bonuses, the Ironquay SOW3 issue and the DD-006 incident. Most of the key risks would become non-claimable. We require **specific, fair disclosure only**: each matter identified against the relevant warranty with enough detail for us to assess its nature and scope. Whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure should all be deleted.

**Paragraph 1.4 (non-admission).** This is acceptable in principle. However, it must not operate to dilute any specific disclosure or override the SPA.

**Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3).** The bar covers anything known to the Buyer *or its advisers*, including matters merely *discoverable* from the data room or public records. **Delete.** In practice it is a second, constructive version of the general disclosure. Combined with paragraph 1.1, it would make the warranties close to worthless. Any knowledge qualifier must:
- apply to the Seller's knowledge, through named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry;
- never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

---

## 4. Completion protections

**Bluefen (cl 3 / 6.3).** This is a critical issue. Bluefen accounts for about AUD 3.6m, or roughly 30%, of FY26 revenue. The Seller's own disclosure confirms there is **no final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied**. The Seller offers reasonable endeavours plus consent-on-delivery, which is insufficient under the playbook. We should require:
- a condition precedent of an **effective** consent, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer;
- **evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied** before Completion;
- an endeavours obligation stronger than reasonable endeavours;
- a Buyer walk-right or long-stop date if the condition is not met.

**Riverlark (cl 2 / 7).** The facility has about AUD 3.2m outstanding. It has not been repaid and no discharge of security has been delivered. The Seller proposes a release "following Completion". **Reject** on a debt-free / cash-free deal. We should require:
- a current payout letter;
- direct repayment out of Completion funds, treated as a Debt deduction in the funds flow;
- executed releases and discharges at Completion, including PPSR and any share security.

A post-completion release would only be possible with an irrevocable undertaking from the lender **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists.

**Employee bonuses (funds flow).** The DD-005 bonuses total AUD 420,000. The Seller calls them "a matter for the Seller", yet the disclosure admits they are not in the funds flow. The Company is the employer, so the liability lands on us after Completion unless it is dealt with. The Seller's own letter also leaves payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs unaddressed. We should require:
- either a specific funds-flow line item (as Debt or a transaction-cost deduction) or Seller funding;
- coverage of triggered on-costs;
- clarification of how the continued-employment conditions operate around Completion.

The funds flow must not exclude these amounts silently.

---

## 5. Specific matters

**Ironquay IP (cl 11.1).** The existing indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment. Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. That figure is **not independently verified either way**, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment. We should:
- broaden the indemnity to cover loss from any failure of the Company to own, or any third-party claim over, the Ironquay materials;
- preserve the SOW3 cure: payment verified, plus a confirmatory assignment, ideally as a Completion deliverable;
- request evidence of the actual payment status.

**DD-006 export / privacy incident.** The Seller calls this "not expected to be material". That is an assertion. Under the playbook we assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric exposure in either direction. We should seek pre-completion covenants requiring the Seller to:
- preserve logs;
- complete the investigation;
- provide regular written updates and give us access;
- consult the Buyer and comply with any notification obligation that is determined to apply.

This matter must not be swept into general disclosure. We should ask for an update since 22 September. Any specific protection should be kept open, with no numbers proposed by either side for now.

**Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000).** The Seller calls them "ordinary-course operating costs". Its own disclosure says it does *not* state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. We should assess the contracts for timing, scope, terminability and the related-party angle the disclosure flags ("read together"). Consistent with the playbook, there should be **no automatic Debt classification or price deduction**. We should also not accept the Seller's characterisation without evidence.

**Title.** DD-012 is the Company's own share register: a supplied internal source, not independent proof. We should require independent evidence, including:
- an ASIC company extract;
- share certificates and the constitution;
- PPSR searches against the Seller and the shares;
- Seller board authority and capacity evidence;
- confirmation that no encumbrance (including any Riverlark security) attaches to the shares.

Title must also sit in the fundamental regime described in section 2.

**Lower-priority items.**
- **DD-007 lease:** this is a notification obligation only. It should be built into the completion steps.
- **DD-009 Mossvale:** this is an assignment restriction that does not on its face bite on a share sale. We should confirm that analysis on full review rather than assume it.

---

## 6. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the framing.** Do not treat "FINAL", "agreed at principal level" or "market standard" as authority. Confirm the position internally with Amelia Frost.
2. **Cap:** 25% / AUD 6.0m. No fallback without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft.
3. **Thresholds:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000, first dollar once exceeded.
4. **General claims period:** 24 months. Strike the "applies to all Claims" catch-all.
5. **Fundamental / Title:** separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and no basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
6. **Fraud carve-out:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct excluded from all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. This is non-negotiable.
7. **Disclosure:** specific fair disclosure only. Delete data-room, register, Accounts and public-records deemed disclosure.
8. **Buyer knowledge:** delete cl 8.3. Any qualifier must be Seller-side, use named persons with reasonable enquiry, and never excuse title, capacity, fraud or indemnities.
9. **Bluefen:** condition precedent of effective consent plus evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion, a stronger endeavours obligation, and a walk-right.
10. **Riverlark:** current payout letter, repayment from Completion funds and releases at Completion. Any post-completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
11. **Bonuses:** AUD 420,000 plus on-costs either itemised in the funds flow or Seller-funded.
12. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and verify payment status.
13. **DD-006:** preservation, investigation, updates and consultation covenants. No assumed breach or quantum.
14. **Sandbar:** assess on evidence. No automatic Debt classification or deduction.
15. **Tax / IP:** keep open and separate. Reject "settled under general regime".
16. **Title:** independent evidence beyond DD-012.
17. **Refresh the record:** request a bring-down of all disclosed matters since 22 September 2026, and distinguish verified updates from assertions.

**Approvals needed before any concession:** Amelia Frost's written authority is required for (a) the 20% cap fallback, (b) the 18-month claims period fallback and (c) any post-completion Riverlark release. The fraud carve-out cannot be waived by anyone.
